hook.text: A pile of uranium sits inert for years. Add just enough material and it triggers a nuclear chain reaction instantly.

buildup.text: Critical mass is the threshold where a system suddenly changes behavior. Below it, nothing. Above it, everything.

discovery.text: Social movements, viral content, and startup growth all follow this pattern. Slow buildup, then explosive takeoff.

twist.text: You cannot tell when you are close to critical mass. The jump from 99 to 100 percent looks the same as 10 to 11.

climax.text: Persistence matters most near the threshold. Many people quit just before the reaction would have started.

punchline.text: Slow, slow, slow, then boom. That is critical mass.

quiz.question: Why do people often give up just before achieving critical mass?
options: The concept doesn't apply to real life
Progress near the threshold looks the same as earlier, so the tipping point is invisible
